title: Ukraine's Drone War Cuts Deep Into Russian Refining: Ust-Luga Terminal Hit, Moscow Now Imports Indian Gasoline
subhead: A Ukrainian drone attack on Russia's top Baltic export port Ust-Luga caps a summer of refinery strikes that have pushed Moscow to import fuel from India and sent diesel exports to multi-year lows — while the US-Iran Hormuz stalemate keeps rerouting global supply.

sections.heading: Ust-Luga Burning: Ukraine's Refining War Reaches Russia's Export Hub
sections.body:
A fire broke out at Ust-Luga, Russia's leading Baltic port for oil, fuel, coal, fertilizer and grain exports, early Friday after an overnight Ukrainian drone attack, Leningrad region governor Alexander Drozdenko said on Telegram. Firefighters worked through the day, with Drozdenko later posting that the attack's consequences were eliminated and there were no victims. OilPrice reports this was not the first strike on Ust-Luga — Ukrainian drones hit the port in early July.

The attack fits a broader campaign: Ukraine struck Gazprom's Neftekhim Salavat complex in the Urals (around 200,000 bpd of refining capacity) on Thursday, according to OilPrice. The cumulative damage has left Russia's refining system badly degraded for over three months, forcing Moscow to curb fuel exports and even import gasoline.
sections.whyItMatters: Ukraine has moved beyond targeting refineries to striking Russia's export terminals themselves, directly attacking the revenue pipeline that funds the war — while degrading the domestic fuel supply that sustains the Russian economy.

sections.heading: Moscow Now Imports Indian Gasoline as Refinery Runs Collapse
sections.body:
Russia has begun importing fuels from India, Bloomberg reported, citing Kpler data showing a 42,000-ton cargo of gasoline from Nayara Energy's Vadinar refinery arriving in Russia on August 5. The refinery is partly owned by Rosneft, which supplies the crude processed there. Kpler lead analyst Sumit Ritolia called the Indian barrels 'particularly notable,' highlighting 'the severity of the current domestic petrol imbalance.'

The scale of the damage is stark: EA Analytics estimates Russia's refinery runs stood at 3.6 million barrels daily in July, over 30% below the seasonal average. Russian diesel and gasoil exports crashed to just 80,000 bpd in the first seven days of August, a multi-year low, OilPrice reports. Seaborne crude exports also fell to their lowest since May as recovering refinery runs pulled barrels back into domestic processing.
sections.whyItMatters: A crude exporter that once supplied India's refiners is now importing finished fuel from a Rosneft-linked Indian plant — a reversal that shows how deeply Ukraine's drone campaign has reshaped global product flows and Russia's place in them.

sections.heading: Hormuz Stalemate Holds as US West Coast Reaches for Malaysian Fuel Oil
sections.body:
With the US-Iran standoff over the Strait of Hormuz unresolved, Brent traded near $87-89 and WTI around $82-84 this week, heading for a roughly 4% weekly gain, OilPrice reports. US commercial crude inventories rose over 17.4 million barrels last week, per ING analysts, but the geopolitical premium kept prices from falling further. Iran says Hormuz stays closed until Washington meets its conditions; President Trump countered that the US has 'total control' of the waterway — 'We own it.'

The rerouting is visible in trade flows. A Malaysian fuel oil cargo aboard the Solomon Sea tanker — over 540,000 barrels of LSSR fuel oil from Petronas' PRefChem refinery — is heading to a US West Coast refinery, the first such shipment since 2023, per Reuters and MarineTraffic data reported by OilPrice. Meanwhile, OilPrice reports Middle East tankers are going dark for longer periods, with transponders off at Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb. Vice President JD Vance said keeping oil and gas cheap is the administration's 'goal number one' in the Iran war, as US national average gasoline stayed above $4 per gallon (AAA).
sections.whyItMatters: The Hormuz closure has widened arbitrage windows enough that US West Coast refiners — normally supplied from Mexico and Venezuela — are pulling LSSR fuel oil from Southeast Asia, a concrete measure of how global product flows are being redrawn by the blockade.

sections.heading: Kazakhstan Accuses Big Oil of $10.7 Billion Corruption at Kashagan
sections.body:
Kazakhstan has alleged in a confidential arbitration case that the consortium developing the giant Kashagan oilfield awarded roughly a dozen contracts in the 2000s with unjustified cost increases or through bribery, the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists (ICIJ) reported, citing multiple sources. The consortium's shareholders include KazMunayGas, Eni, Shell, ExxonMobil, TotalEnergies, China's CNPC and Japan's INPEX.

ICIJ reports the corruption claim is part of a larger $160 billion claim from Kazakhstan over lost production, profits and environmental damage, registered with the Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague, where no decision has yet been made. OilPrice notes Kazakhstan has multiple arbitration cases totaling up to $166 billion against the majors.
sections.whyItMatters: Astana is escalating its fight with the Western and Asian majors that built its flagship offshore project — a signal that resource nationalism is hardening in Central Asia even as the region's crude faces export constraints through Russia and the disrupted Caspian corridor.

sections.heading: Indonesia Quake Hits Fuel Distribution as Asia's Demand Picture Grows
sections.body:
A 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck eastern Flores Island on Saturday, killing at least 47 people and prompting a 14-day emergency response status through Aug. 28, Anadolu Agency reported. State-owned Pertamina said 32 gas stations in the region were operating while 20 remained closed due to damage; fuel and LPG supplies across Flores were being restored as search-and-rescue continued. President Prabowo Subianto oversaw the dispatch of 27 tons of supplies.

On the demand side, Indian government projections cited by OilPrice see India's coal demand jumping to 1.6 billion tons by 2030, from about 1.2 billion tons now, on higher electricity generation and industrial activity — a reminder that Asia's structural energy appetite is rising even amid the IEA and OPEC demand downgrades driven by the war and high prices.
sections.whyItMatters: The quake tests Indonesia's fuel logistics resilience at a moment of global product tightness, while India's coal trajectory underscores the disconnect between Western transition timelines and Asian demand growth that IEA and OPEC forecasts are now trying to reconcile.

bottomLine: The defining shift this week is inside Russia: Ukraine's drone campaign has moved from refineries to export terminals, pushing Moscow to import Indian gasoline, crash its diesel exports to multi-year lows, and run refineries 30% below seasonal norms — an exporter now importing finished fuel. Meanwhile the US-Iran Hormuz stalemate grinds on with Brent above $87, visibly rerouting global trade (US West Coast pulling Malaysian fuel oil for the first time since 2023) even as Washington frames cheap American gasoline as its top war goal. Kazakhstan's $160 billion arbitration push against the Kashagan majors and Indonesia's quake-hit fuel network round out a day where supply disruption, not diplomacy, set the tone.
sources: OilPrice.com (Paraskova, Kennedy, Slav), Bloomberg via OilPrice (Kpler data), Reuters, ICIJ via OilPrice, Anadolu Agency, ING, EA Analytics, AAA
